class.name: NetwDisplayRuntime
class.brief_description: Everything one entity's display pump reads and writes for a frame.
class.description:
One of these per displayed entity. It carries the entity's channels, the playhead they are sampled through, the role the pump was resolved for, and the bookkeeping a pass needs to tell a stalled display from one being driven to a constant. The entity and its owner node are held by instance id and resolved on each read, so a runtime that outlives either answers [code]null[/code] and the pass declines rather than following a pointer. [codeblock] var runtime := NetwDisplayRuntime.new() runtime.route = route runtime.bind(entity, entity.owner) runtime.config = decl runtime.playhead = NetwDisplayPlayhead.new()
if runtime.pump_mode == NetwDisplayDecl.PUMP_UNRESOLVED: resolve_role(runtime) for channel in runtime.states: pump(channel) [/codeblock] [member pump_mode] and [member role] are two answers, not one: two roles share the bracketed pump, so the pump alone cannot say which one is running. Role resolution is event-driven — liveness, control, reparenting, config rebuilds and every network record — so a pass resolves only a runtime that has never been resolved and never scans authority per frame.

method.name: authoring_tick
method.description: The authoring tick the display is currently standing on, or [code]-1[/code]. Answered by the first channel that carries the authoring stamp, read at [member playhead]'s display tick: a display is showing a moment, and that moment's tick is what a caller comparing display against simulation needs. [code]-1[/code] when no set authors this entity, when the playhead has not placed yet, and when no authoring channel has a sample behind the playhead.

method.name: bind
method.description: Binds the entity this runtime displays and the node its channels are sampled from. Neither is kept alive by the binding, and neither dangles.

method.name: buffer_of
method.description: The recorded samples behind [param track], or [code]null[/code]. A chase pump answers nothing whatever the track: it eases toward a live body rather than sampling a history, so a buffer read there would hand a caller a ring the display is not showing from.

method.name: channel_named
method.description: The channel [param name] addresses, or [code]null[/code] when no channel claimed it. Addressed by NAME through [member tracks], which is the property a caller holds, never by the channel's own key. A name two channels declared answers whichever declared first, and says so once. Two channels answering to one name is an authoring mistake, not a lookup mode.

method.name: reset
method.description: Restarts every channel from the live source: the playhead settles to [param display_offset], each channel forgets its recorded samples and held offset, and the value on the source right now is shown and taken as the value the next pass eases from. This is what a teleport of the whole entity is. A reset that kept the history would glide back through the poses it just left, one channel at a time.

method.name: snap_named
method.description: Snaps the channel [param name] addresses to [param value], through [method NetwDisplayChannel.snap]. A name no channel claimed is a no-op, because a display that shows nothing under that name has nothing to teleport.

method.name: entity
method.description: The bound entity, or [code]null[/code] once it has been freed.

method.name: owner
method.description: The bound owner node, or [code]null[/code] once it has been freed.

method.name: track_stat
method.description: One display diagnostic, or [code]null[/code] when [param stat] names none. [code]sleeping[/code], [code]buffer[/code] and [code]buffer_size[/code] answer about [param track]; [code]channels[/code], [code]ambiguous[/code], [code]pumped_frames[/code], [code]starvation_ticks[/code] and [code]display_lag[/code] answer about the whole runtime and ignore it. These are diagnostics rather than law: a display that is not behaving is read here instead of being re-derived from the pump.

members.member: The declared set whose frames carry the tick-ack stamp, which is the single authoring stream the displayed tick is read from. Null when no set authors one.
The recovery-absorption subscription, held only while the chase pump runs.
What the entity declared about how it is displayed.

The display tick past which a timed disable re-enables this runtime, or [code]-1[/code] when the disable is not timed. This is the tick-space replacement for a scene-tree timer, so a paused session does not run the window down.
Whether the pump skips this runtime entirely.

The largest render offset a chase absorption may hold, which is the entity's own teleport tier. Infinite until a role resolution reads one, because an entity that declares no teleport threshold is entitled to glide any distance.
The control-changed and reparented subscriptions, held for the runtime's life.
Where in recorded time this entity is being shown. Minted with the runtime, so no caller has to remember to and no pass can meet a runtime that has nowhere to read from.

Which pump drives this runtime, one of [NetwDisplayDecl]'s [code]PUMP_*[/code] values. [constant NetwDisplayDecl.PUMP_UNRESOLVED] until a role resolution answers, which is what makes the resolve event-driven rather than per frame.
How many passes this runtime has actually taken, which is what tells a stalled display apart from one the pump is driving to a constant.
Whether a channel-table rebuild is already scheduled for the session's settle, so a cascade of config writes costs one rebuild.
The role [member pump_mode] was chosen for. Two roles share the bracketed pump, so the pump alone cannot answer which one is running.
The session route this runtime's entity was enrolled under.
What a body's freeze state was before a remote role froze it, so restoring the role restores the body rather than guessing at a default.
The channels this entity is displayed through, in declaration order.
Which channel a track resolves to, by either of a channel's two names. Minted with the runtime.
The last frame this runtime emitted a trace on, so tracing costs one line per frame rather than one per channel.
Whether the self-feedback warning has already fired, so it warns once per runtime rather than once per role resolution.
